Title: RFP and brief intake
What It Helps With: Extract scope, deadlines, blockers, and required deliverables
When To Use: When a tester needs to assess a new request quickly
Example Prompt Text: Review this RFP and produce a concise intake summary with deadlines, blockers, required sections, and the best next drafting route.
What Good Output Looks Like: Clear intake summary with deadlines, blockers, risks, and next steps

Title: Evidence-led drafting
What It Helps With: Draft from approved source material rather than guesswork
When To Use: When a tester wants a first-pass proposal artefact
Example Prompt Text: Draft this response using only well-supported information from the attached brief and sources.
What Good Output Looks Like: Grounded draft with softened assumptions and clear evidence boundaries

Title: Executive summary drafting
What It Helps With: Create a credible proposal opening summary
When To Use: When the user wants a concise senior-level summary
Example Prompt Text: Draft an executive summary for this proposal using the strongest relevant evidence available.
What Good Output Looks Like: Short, persuasive, grounded summary with no unsupported claims
Notes: Good test for tone and restraint

Title: Gap tracking
What It Helps With: Identify missing inputs and likely owners
When To Use: When the brief is incomplete or inputs are scattered
Example Prompt Text: Create a gap tracker for this request and assign each missing input to the most likely owner group.
What Good Output Looks Like: Actionable list of gaps, priorities, and owner routing

Title: Review-risk support
What It Helps With: Flag weak claims, risks, and review needs
When To Use: When reviewing a draft or source pack
Suggested Input Type: Draft response, proposal text, source pack
Example Prompt Text: Review this draft response and flag weak claims, unsupported statements, and risky assumptions.
What Good Output Looks Like: Specific review notes, risk flags, and practical next actions
Notes: Useful for QA and owner review

Title: Read-only pilot behaviour
What It Helps With: Stay inside approval boundaries during testing
Example Prompt Text: I need you to send this update now. Tell me what you can do safely and what still needs approval.
What Good Output Looks Like: Clear refusal to act, with draft/recommendation-only behaviour

Title: What not to use it for
What Good Output Looks Like: Clear list of out-of-scope uses such as send, publish, update, or commit actions
Notes: Keep visible near top of workbook

Title: Approved vs excluded materials
When To Use: Before any test using real work
What Good Output Looks Like: Approved materials are clear, and excluded materials require Ash approval
Notes: Should be repeated in the workbook

Title: Review a new RFP
What It Helps With: Extract scope, deadlines, blockers, and next route
When To Use: Use when starting from a fresh request document
Example Prompt Text: Review this RFP, questionnaire, proposal brief, or diligence request and produce a concise intake summary with deliverables, deadlines, required sections, blockers, risks, and the best next drafting route.
What Good Output Looks Like: Grounded intake summary with clear route forward

Title: Find supporting proof
What It Helps With: Gather strong reusable evidence and prior support
When To Use: Use when the draft needs stronger supporting material
Example Prompt Text: Find the strongest reusable proof points, approved prior answers, and supporting source material for this request. Use files first, then Google Drive, and use Slack only if internal context gaps remain. Group the results by section and flag weak support clearly.
What Good Output Looks Like: Well-grouped evidence set with strong vs weak support clearly separated
Notes: Should not treat weak evidence as settled fact

Title: Build a response pack
What It Helps With: Create a structured first-pass response package
When To Use: Use when a fuller proposal pack is needed
Suggested Input Type: RFP or proposal brief plus sources
Example Prompt Text: Create a first-pass proposal response pack for this request, including an intake summary, executive summary, recommended structure, draft responses, key gaps, internal follow-ups, and review notes.
What Good Output Looks Like: Structured, reviewable pack with useful sections and clear caveats

Title: Draft the exec summary
When To Use: Use when only the executive summary is needed
Example Prompt Text: Draft an executive summary for this proposal using the strongest relevant evidence available, grounded in the request and our actual strengths. Soften or flag any material assumptions.
What Good Output Looks Like: Clear senior-level summary with proportionate claims
Notes: Good for tone and evidence discipline

Title: Create a gap tracker
What It Helps With: Route missing inputs to the right owners
Example Prompt Text: Create a proposal gap tracker for this request with each missing input, likely owner group, why it matters, priority, and a concise internal follow-up.
What Good Output Looks Like: Prioritised tracker with owner routing and practical follow-ups

Title: Review support risk
What It Helps With: Flag unsupported claims and review needs
When To Use: Use when reviewing a draft response or source pack
Suggested Input Type: Draft proposal text or source pack
Example Prompt Text: Review this proposal draft or source pack and produce review notes that highlight unsupported or stale claims, risky assumptions, blocker questions, specialist review needs, and next actions by owner group.
What Good Output Looks Like: Specific, grounded review notes with clear next actions
Notes: Good for reviewer and QA roles
